deferred_source_units.reason: The unit says those doing lawlessness did not walk in God’s ways. A more particular comparison beyond the general opposition of wrongdoing and the divine way was not established; it is not treated as a report about a named group.

The resolution to keep ordinances ends in a plea not to be forsaken utterly. The actual reading did not establish a distinctive counterpart beyond this conventional obedience-and-nonabandonment appeal.

Wholehearted seeking accompanies a request not to be thrust away from commandments. The unusual requested restraint is preserved; it is not changed into the familiar petition against wandering, and no sufficiently specific corresponding action was established.
The unit blesses the Lord and asks teaching of ordinances. This common instructional petition did not establish a particular connection beyond shared devotion and teaching language.

The lips declared all judgments of God’s mouth. The speaking of divine judgments was read as stated, but no counterpart specific enough to this lips-and-divine-mouth declaration was retained merely from generic religious speech.

Pondering commandments and considering God’s ways are stated together. Their general combination within the poem did not by itself establish a distinctive comparison beyond recurring meditation on instruction.
The speaker promises meditation on ordinances and not forgetting words. A separately particular connection was not retained simply from the common remember-and-meditate formula.

The Gimal opening asks recompense for the servant and anticipates living and keeping the words. The plea’s particular relation of recompense and continued life was not identified with a specific reward promise or event.

The soul longed to desire judgments at every time. No particular comparison beyond sustained longing for divine instruction was established, and the unusual desire-to-desire formulation is not simplified into an unexpressed image.
The speaker declared his ways, was heard and asks teaching. No particular counterpart to this sequence was established; declaring ways is not assumed to be a confession of a specified sin.

The request is to remove the way of injustice and show mercy through the law. A shared request to remove something bad was insufficient to identify a specific counterpart to this law-and-mercy formulation.
The speaker chose the way of truth and did not forget judgments. No distinctive corresponding scene or verbal structure beyond general truthful obedience was established.
The plea asks understanding so the speaker can search the law and keep it with the whole heart. Broad associations between understanding and observance alone were not retained for this unit.
Guidance in the desired path of commandments is requested. Beyond the poem’s recurring moral-path language, a sufficiently particular additional comparison was not established in this pass.

Desired commandments accompany a plea for life in righteousness. The shared themes of righteousness and life in other prayers were not enough to establish a particular counterpart to this combined appeal.

Keeping the law continually and for age upon age is promised. An eternal status assigned to divine words elsewhere is not simply identical to this speaker’s promised duration of observance, and no more particular link was retained.
The speaker reports meditating on commandments greatly loved. This common love-and-meditation conjunction alone did not yield a sufficiently particular comparison beyond the poem’s general subject.

The Zai opening asks remembrance of the word that caused the servant to hope. The saying is not identified; equating it with the dynastic promise to David remains a separate read but unresolved candidate.
This became mine because I sought the ordinances has an unspecified this. The antecedent was not resolved into a particular event, gift or promise to manufacture a cross-reference.

The actual wording reports being prepared and not troubled to keep commandments. It does not say hastened or did not delay; no particular target for the supplied preparation-and-tranquility formulation was established.
The speaker says God dealt kindly with His servant according to the word. No particular promise or narrated kindness was identified from this general acknowledgement of faithful treatment.
God’s goodness grounds a request to be taught ordinances. The common goodness-and-instruction appeal was not enough by itself to establish a distinctive relationship.
Compassion is requested so the speaker may live, with the law as meditation. A particular connection beyond shared compassion, life and devotion was not established.

The arrogant are to be ashamed for unjust lawlessness while the speaker promises to ponder commandments. No identifiable encounter or distinctive counterpart beyond a common opposition of wrongdoers and fidelity was established.

The speaker asks how many the servant’s days are and when judgment against pursuers will occur. No stated duration, identified pursuit or particular judgment episode resolves these questions; no chronology was inferred.

Lawbreakers told idle tales, but not in keeping with the law. They are not described as digging pits in this edition. Whether their tales are the same kind of stories rejected in 1 Timothy remains a separate unresolved comparison.

The source says they nearly brought the speaker to an end on earth but did not forsake commandments. No particular historical threat or sufficiently distinct matching rescue episode was established from this report.

The speaker saw an end to every completion and calls the commandment exceedingly broad. Completion’s precise referent and the proposed comparison with Zophar’s questions about divine extremes remain unresolved; limitless-command language was not supplied.
The speaker did not turn from judgments because God instructed him. A particular relationship beyond general divine teaching and persevering obedience was not established.
God is called helper and upholder and the word is the object of hope. No more distinctive counterpart beyond common support-and-hope prayer language was established.

Help is requested, and salvation and continual meditation on ordinances are anticipated. This conventional aid-and-observance pattern was not treated as a particular historical or literary link by itself.

The speaker reckoned all sinners as transgressors and therefore loved testimonies. The unit does not describe God removing people like dross; no counterpart to the actual speaker’s reckoning was established.

The speaker claims to have done judgment and righteousness and asks not to be handed to wrongdoers. No particular adjudicated case or sufficiently distinctive parallel beyond a general claim of just conduct was established.
Merciful treatment of the servant and teaching of ordinances are requested. A link was not retained solely from that common mercy-and-instruction combination.
The servant asks understanding to know the testimonies. The unit supplies no distinct circumstance or image beyond the repeated instructional plea sufficient for a particular retained relationship.

The speaker opened his mouth and drew breath in longing for commandments. This is not silently converted into eating a scroll or being fed words; no sufficiently specific counterpart to the actual breathing action was established.

The request asks God to look and show mercy according to judgment for lovers of His name. A general association of love for God and mercy was not enough to establish a more particular counterpart to this formulation.
The speaker calls the Lord righteous and His judgment upright. A separately distinctive connection beyond these broad declarations of divine justice was not retained.

Everlasting righteousness of testimonies is followed by a plea for understanding and anticipation of life. No particular counterpart beyond the general combination of instruction, righteousness and life was established.
A wholehearted cry asks hearing and promises seeking the ordinances. No distinctive historical or literary connection beyond this common complete-hearted prayer pattern was established.
The speaker cried for salvation and promised to keep testimonies. A particular counterpart beyond the common rescue-and-observance appeal was not established.

The voice is to be heard according to mercy and life given according to judgment. A shared request for hearing or mercy alone did not establish a sufficiently particular counterpart to the paired grounds in this unit.
The Lord’s many compassions ground a plea for life according to judgment. No particular instance of compassion or distinct matching event was identified from this general prayer.
Many pursuers and those pressing hard are contrasted with not turning from testimonies. Their number and pressure do not identify an episode, and a broad many-enemies comparison was not retained.
The speaker asks God to see his love of commandments and give life in mercy. No more distinctive correspondence beyond the repeated loyalty-and-life petition was established.
Awaiting salvation and loving commandments are stated together. No distinct temporal event or specific counterpart beyond this general conjunction of hope and fidelity was established.
The soul kept testimonies and loved them greatly. This unqualified statement of loving observance did not establish a particular relationship beyond the poem’s recurring subject.

The Thau opening asks supplication to draw near and understanding according to God’s saying. A sufficiently particular connection beyond the conventional approach-and-understanding prayer was not established.

The plea is to enter before God and deliverance to come according to the saying. No particular saying or promised deliverance is identified, and the parallel prayer syntax alone was not used for additional credit.
The speaker asks God’s hand to save because he chose commandments. No specified saving act or more distinctive hand image was established beyond a conventional divine-help appeal.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved identification of the remembered servant-word with the Davidic house promise
unresolved_candidates.rationale: Psalm 118 does not name David, a house or offspring in its request to remember the word that caused hope. The fully read prayer in 2 Samuel explicitly concerns David’s house. Similar servant-and-word language supports no identification of that unnamed saying as this particular dynastic promise.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved classification of the lawbreakers’ idle tales
unresolved_candidates.rationale: Psalm 118 says lawbreakers told idle tales, but not in keeping with the law. First Timothy rejects profane and old women’s myths. The contents of the tales are not given, so a shared identified class of stories or particular literary dependence is not established merely by disparaging narrative labels.

unresolved_candidates.relationship: Unresolved relationship of completion and breadth to divine extremes
unresolved_candidates.rationale: Psalm 118 contrasts an end seen to every completion with an exceedingly broad commandment. Zophar asks about finding a trace of the Lord or reaching the furthest things the Almighty made, then invokes height, depth, length and the sea’s breadth. The shared dimensional terms do not resolve what completion means or justify equating the commandment with Zophar’s unsearchable objects.
